Hi Liam — thanks for sending this over and for the clear checklist. Looping in Marissa (Security & Compliance) and Ben (Solutions) to make sure we cover both controls and implementation tradeoffs.

Quick summary up front: yes, we can support tenant-scoped retention windows in EU regions and provide multiple redaction strategies. The right path depends on which downstream capabilities you need to preserve (search/indexing, embeddings, model fine-tuning). High-level options:

- Retain-and-mask (field-level masking): fast to implement, searchable metadata kept, low cost. Not irreversible by default unless you apply a one-way transform.
- Pseudonymize (token mapping): preserves referential integrity for analytics; reversible if you hold keys. Meets many compliance needs but adds key-management scope (KMS/HSM).
- Irreversible hash/drop (strong sanitization): best for irreversibility but breaks identity joins and most ML features.

Marissa / Ben — can you add the specifics about logs and audit artifacts we can hand over? Liam, I'll follow with a short two-page options doc and a checklist mapping to your list.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

> Quick summary up front: yes, we can support tenant-scoped retention windows in EU regions and provide multiple redaction strategies.

Liam — adding some technical detail and tradeoffs so you have something concrete for Legal/Engineering:

1) Tenant-scoped retention: we offer per-tenant retention policy enforcement that runs asynchronously on storage and index layers. Retention windows can be configured by day (e.g., 6y = 2190 days) and applied to message/document classes. Purge runs are auditable and produce a signed deletion manifest (timestamp, object IDs, initiator).

2) Redaction modalities we can deploy at cutover:
   - Field mask: replace sensitive fields with structured placeholders (e.g., [REDACTED_NAME]). Keeps doc shape and most search indices intact. Reversible only if you keep original content in an isolated vault (not recommended).
   - Token mapping service (pseudonymization): we can spin up a tenant-scoped mapping store with KMS-backed encryption for reference IDs. Tradeoff: reversible if key + map retained; requires rotation and key governance.
   - One-way hashing + salt: irreversible if you use per-tenant salt and discard it. Good for identifiers (SSNs, MRNs) but destroys semantic content for embeddings.
   - Selective KV-cache deletion: for hosted inference, KV caches for recent sessions are purged on request; we can target caches older than X days during cutover to avoid leakage.

3) Auditor artifacts:
   - Deletion manifests (signed)
   - Redaction audit events (who/what/when) with hashes of original object ids
   - Sample transformed artifacts and transformation code snippets (statements of irreversible hash used)

4) Search and ML implications:
   - If you need embeddings or semantic search to continue to work on redacted content, prefer pseudonymization or field mask + supplemental synthetic replacement.
   - If you require cryptographic irreversibility, you lose meaningful embeddings and joins — plan for analytic workarounds.

I attached a short deck and a compliance checklist that maps to your bulleted asks. Proposed next step: a joint call next week (30 min) with Careline engineering and Redwood security to pick the final approach and record acceptance criteria for the cutover runbook.

Attaching: data-retention-options-v2.pdf, redaction-checklist.xlsx

Ben Carter

Liam — thanks for the detailed questions. Legal note up front: Careline's ask for a 6-year retention window is acceptable from a controls perspective; we'll need an LOA that defines accountable roles and data categories. Operational guidance below:

- Evidence and artifacts: we will produce deletion manifests, redaction audit logs, and sample transformed outputs. These artifacts will include immutable timestamps and signer metadata. We can also provide an automated export for auditors on demand (S3/drive link) for a defined retention period after cutover.

- Recommended default configuration for cutover (Redwood-hosted, EU region):
   * Retention window: 6 years (tenant-scoped)
   * Redaction: use per-field irreversible hash for direct identifiers (SSN/MRN) + pseudonymization for linking IDs needed for analytics. Keep a separate pseudonymization mapping under KMS control.
   * KV-cache policy: purge session caches older than 30 days at cutover + continuous KV sweep for 90 days.

- Audit readiness: we'll provide a short SOC2-style evidence bundle and a template statement you can include with your auditors. Please have Legal sign the attached LOA / acceptance so we can enable tenant-scoped KMS and mapping store.

I'll schedule the joint call for next Wednesday; Soojin, please loop in Careline engineering contact Ayesha (copied on thread) if available.
